source.title: Information-Theoretic Scaling Laws for Generative Diffusion Training
source.authors: Druv Pai; Dejan Stancevic; Y. Ma; Luca Ambrogioni

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports scaling results for diffusion-model information, memorization, and image quality, not the held-out language-model loss or compute-allocation quantities in the claim versions. It mentions language-model scaling laws in related work but does not test or rely on them.
record.gate_note: The paper’s scaling experiments measure model information and its relationships to image memorization and FID, rather than language-model cross-entropy loss, downstream task performance, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Those results are recorded as related findings with versions ["none"]. References to Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al. are background citations and are not treated as results.
record.test_reason: The study measures model information, the mutual information between a trained diffusion model and its samples, plus memorization ratio and FID. It does this for small image-diffusion UNets across training-set size N and model size P. It never measures held-out pretraining loss or downstream task performance, and it does not vary compute allocation or architecture shape at fixed P. Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al. appear only as a one-sentence related-work citation. Image diffusion is a different modality, but the scaled quantity is not loss, so V5 is not tested either. 'cites_only' fits better than 'discusses', since there is no argument about the language-model laws.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: model information can be estimated from a few trained models and scales predictably across training-set size and model capacity. It tracks memorization below Nc(P) and FID above it, enabling predictions of memorization and sample quality at unseen settings.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains unconditional image diffusion models and measures model information, memorization, and FID; it does not use language-model pretraining-loss measurements or fixed-compute parameter/token allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The model-information estimates vary with the number of reference models: fewer reference models give slightly larger estimates, while fitted scaling parameters change less. The mixture-score estimator also matters: the two classifier estimators give stable fits across tested Ktrain values, while the distilled estimator differs at small Ktrain.

fits_no_version.finding: On ImageNet the proposed model-information law fits with log RMSE 0.112, and the N^-1 regime has slopes from -0.91 to -1.02 across model sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Diffusion model information follows a Marchenko–Pastur-derived law with a fixed N^-1 tail in the generalization regime.

fits_no_version.finding: The same law fits CIFAR-10, Fashion-MNIST and FFHQ with log RMSE 0.101, 0.074 and 0.109.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The model-information law transfers across image datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Fits on L∈{2,3,4} predict model information, memorization ratio and FID at L=5, N=250,000: 235/221 nats, 0/0, and 33.5/28.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induced memorization and FID laws extrapolate to a withheld model size.

fits_no_version.finding: FID is non-monotone in N: it peaks near Nc(P) just after memorization stops, then falls in the N^-1 regime. FID regressions fitted on all N predict much worse (log RMSE 0.285 vs 0.066).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sample-quality scaling in diffusion models is non-monotone across the memorization transition, so naive monotone fits fail.

fits_no_version.finding: A sigmoid–power form with a free N exponent fits α=0.15 on ImageNet, far from the measured slope near -1, and gives a poor F(P) (Table 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fitted exponents of model-information laws depend strongly on the chosen functional form.

record.code_released: GitHub is stated, but no URL is given in the text.
record.problems: The empirical study uses four trained models per (P,N) pair for most datasets, and the authors note that model-information estimates have finite-reference-model, score-estimation, quadrature, and terminal-remainder errors. Some measurements are presented in figures rather than fully tabulated.
record.rows_left_out: Individual model-information, memorization, and FID measurements across the full (P,N) sweeps are not separately transcribed; they appear mainly as plotted series in Figures 3, 5, 7, 9–11, and 13–14. The rows record the reported aggregate fit results and the explicit withheld-setting predictions.

untested.parts: No held-out loss is measured against parameters, tokens or compute.
Extrapolation is tested only for model information, memorization and FID, not for loss.
There is no fixed-compute allocation of parameters versus data.
Depth and width co-vary with P (h=32L); there is no comparison of shapes at fixed P.
The models are image diffusion models, but there is no power law in loss; the scaled quantity is model information.
FID is related to model information, not to pretraining loss or to downstream tasks.
Functional-form and estimator sensitivity are studied for model information, not for loss exponents or compute-optimal splits.

record.verdict_notes: The two original sources are cited only in related work. No row links to any version. The relation was corrected from 'discusses' to 'cites_only'.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not measure held-out language-model pretraining loss against parameters, tokens, or compute.
It extrapolates diffusion model information, memorization, and FID, not language-model loss.
It does not vary or optimize parameter and token allocations under a fixed compute budget.
It does not compare depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count for language-model loss.

It studies image diffusion models, but its measured quantity is model information rather than the claimed loss-scaling relationship; it does not test the same law for loss across modalities or training regimes.
FID and memorization are not downstream-task performance or downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss.
The paper examines fit and estimator choices for its model-information scaling law, not the setup dependence of language-model loss exponents or compute-optimal allocations.
